newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds may test lower next week after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: Bunds may test lower next week after volatile day.

text.p: Bund futures were nearly unchanged late in the day on Friday after seesawing when the U.S. unemployment report sent mixed signals about the strength of the U.S. economy.
Bunds had been weaker much of the day after stronger-than-expected economic reports this week had hurt the market's outlook and the market may now resume a lower path next week, traders said.
At 1422 GMT, the DTB June Bund futures contract was down a single basis point at 101.68, but had traded in a wide range between 101.32-101.87.

With U.S. jobs out of the way, traders expect the market to refocus on factors that have weighed on it much of the week -- a correction after strong gains this year and healthier-than-expected economic data the last several days.
"This week brought first signs indicating that the German economy is on the verge of a turn-around," said Adolf Rosenstock, economist at the Industrial Bank of Japan.
Analysts said they see intermediate support for the futures contract at around 101.50, a level that corresponds to a support level on the old March contract.
That level was broken several times on the day, but Bunds always climbed back. Below 101.50, the next major support point is the psychologically important level of 101.00.

Finance minister Theo Waigel offered his now customary reassurances on EMU, saying in Munich that the euro would eliminate speculative pressure on the mark. There was little market impact to the remarks.

After a heavy week of indicators, no major economic releases are expected next week. Three Bundesbank council members, however, will speak on Monday including Dieter Kuehbacher, Ernst Welteke and Guntram Palm.
By late in the day, the Benchmark cash Bund down to 102.21 from 102.41 to yield 5.69 percent.
The DTB, meanwhile, launched a new two-year debt futures contract on Friday to upbeat reviews from traders who see the product plugging a hole in the German futures yield curve.

Analysts said that within a couple weeks, they see daily volume in the contract swelling to around 20,000 -- a level of liquidity sufficient to call the contract a success. The contract had volume of 13,000 late in the day on Friday.
The next major U.S. statistic will be labour cost figures for the fourth quarter which are due at 1500 on Tuesday.
Traders said they see further room for Bunds to continue outperforming their U.S. counterparts next week if there are any further signs of a strong U.S. economy.
The spread had climbed to 111 basis points late in the day on Friday from 103 basis points at the previous close.
